fields.label: WPS No. / supporting PQR
fields.ex: Every qualified WPS must name the PQR or PQRs that support it. An inspector checks this link first: a WPS with no PQR behind it (and not prequalified) is just a piece of paper.

fields.label: Process
fields.ex: Changing the process (say GMAW to FCAW) needs its own qualification. Under ASME IX the GMAW transfer mode counts too: spray and short-circuit need separate PQRs (QW-409.2).

fields.label: Joint design
fields.value: Single-V groove, 60°, 1/8 in root opening, steel backing
fields.ex: For an ASME IX procedure, groove design is a nonessential variable (QW-402.1): revise the WPS, no new PQR. Removing the backing does matter for the welder's own qualification.

fields.label: Base metal
fields.value: P-No. 1 to P-No. 1 · up to 3/4 in (3/8 in PQR coupon)
fields.ex: A change of P-Number (QW-403.11), or thickness outside the range the coupon qualified, needs a new PQR. Under QW-451.1 a 3/8 in coupon qualifies up to 2T = 3/4 in.

fields.label: Filler metal
fields.ex: A change of F-Number (QW-404.4) or of weld-metal analysis A-Number (QW-404.5) is essential. Wire diameter is usually nonessential, so it only has to be listed on the WPS.

fields.label: Position
fields.ex: For the PROCEDURE, ASME IX says a qualification in any position qualifies all positions unless notch-toughness rules apply (QW-203). The WELDER is different: position is a performance essential variable, so each welder needs a WPQ that covers it. D1.1 handles positions differently, so check its tables.

fields.label: Preheat / interpass
fields.ex: Under ASME IX, a preheat more than 100 °F below the PQR value is an essential change (QW-406.1). Preheat slows cooling and drives off moisture, which is how it fights hydrogen cracking.

fields.label: Post-weld heat treatment
fields.ex: Adding, removing or changing PWHT changes the metal's properties, so it is essential (QW-407.1) and needs a new PQR.

fields.label: Shielding gas
fields.ex: For GMAW and GTAW, changing the gas or the mix percentages is essential (QW-408.2). A different flow rate inside a listed range is not.

fields.label: Electrical
fields.ex: Welding anywhere inside these ranges follows the WPS. Amperage and voltage are usually nonessential for the procedure, but when notch toughness is required heat input becomes a supplementary essential variable (QW-409.1), and current type or polarity matters for some processes.

fields.label: Travel speed / technique
fields.ex: Usually nonessential, so staying inside the range is enough. Speed still sets heat input: faster travel puts less heat into each inch, which matters when toughness is controlled.
